import torch
import torch.nn as nn


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W0 = 64
        W = 48
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W0, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W0, W0, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W0, W, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(W, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        place = self.place_head(f).flatten(1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r1c3
trials.name: Footprint max/min pooled head
trials.hypothesis: Each brick type gets its own head. It reads learned features max- and min-pooled over that brick's footprint, so it can learn whether all covered cells are missing and level, which is what decides where a brick lands. The heads' output layers start at zero, so the untrained policy is uniform. This should beat the 0.116 baseline mean. It is refuted if the 2-seed mean stays at or below about 0.12.

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

W = 64
H = 32


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W, W, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.ctx = nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1)
        heads = []
        for _ in self.fps:
            out = nn.Conv2d(H, 1, 1)
            nn.init.zeros_(out.weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(out.bias)
            heads.append(nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(2 * W, H, 1), nn.ReLU(), out))
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList(heads)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, W), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(W, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(W, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        h = self.stem(obs)
        f = F.relu(h + self.ctx(h))
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            p = F.pad(f, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            mx = F.max_pool2d(p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            mn = -F.max_pool2d(-p, (dy, dx), stride=1)
            outs.append(head(torch.cat([mx, mn], dim=1)).flatten(1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

trials.label: r2c3
trials.name: Layer-wise footprint heads
trials.hypothesis: Features are computed per layer, with weights shared across layers. Inputs are each cell's channels at layers z-1, z and z+1, a one-hot layer code and a whole-column per-cell feature. Each brick type then gets a learned conv shaped like its footprint, scoring the placement as if it landed at layer z. A soft maximum over z combines them. This matches the landing rule (a brick is right if its footprint is level and missing at one layer) at about the starting compute. Refuted if the mean is at or below 0.20.
trials.code:
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

C = 64
L = 32
H = 16


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        self.Z = spec.Z
        self.fps = [(int(fp[0]), int(fp[1])) for fp in spec.footprints]
        self.stem = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, C, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(C, C, 1), nn.ReLU())
        self.col_proj = nn.Conv2d(C, L, 1)
        self.loc_in = nn.Conv2d(12 + spec.Z, L, 1)
        self.loc2 = nn.Conv2d(L, L, 1)
        self.register_buffer("zpos", torch.eye(spec.Z).view(1, spec.Z, spec.Z, 1, 1))
        heads = []
        for dy, dx in self.fps:
            out = nn.Conv2d(H, 1, 1)
            nn.init.zeros_(out.weight)
            nn.init.zeros_(out.bias)
            heads.append(nn.Sequential(nn.Conv2d(L, H, (dy, dx)), nn.ReLU(), out))
        self.heads = nn.ModuleList(heads)
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * C + 2 * L, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.weight)
        nn.init.zeros_(self.done_head.bias)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        B, _, Y, X = obs.shape
        Z = self.Z
        layers = obs[:, :4 * Z].reshape(B, 4, Z, Y, X).transpose(1, 2)
        below = F.pad(layers, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1, 0))[:, :Z]
        above = F.pad(layers, (0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 1))[:, 1:]
        zp = self.zpos.expand(B, Z, Z, Y, X)
        x = torch.cat([below, layers, above, zp], dim=2).reshape(B * Z, 12 + Z, Y, X)
        col = self.stem(obs)
        cp = self.col_proj(col)
        h = self.loc_in(x).view(B, Z, L, Y, X) + cp.unsqueeze(1)
        h = F.relu(h).reshape(B * Z, L, Y, X)
        h = F.relu(self.loc2(h))
        outs = []
        for fp, head in zip(self.fps, self.heads):
            dy, dx = fp
            p = F.pad(h, (0, dx - 1, 0, dy - 1))
            s = head(p).view(B, Z, Y * X)
            outs.append(torch.logsumexp(s, dim=1))
        place = torch.cat(outs, dim=1)
        hz = h.view(B, Z, L, Y, X)
        g = torch.cat([col.mean((2, 3)), col.amax((2, 3)),
                       hz.mean((1, 3, 4)), hz.amax((1, 3, 4))], dim=1)
        g = self.glob(g)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.nn.functional as F

RECIPE = {"ppo_epochs": 2, "n_envs": 128, "n_minibatches": 16}


class Net(nn.Module):
    def __init__(self, spec):
        super().__init__()
        W0 = 64
        W = 48
        self.body = nn.Sequential(
            nn.Conv2d(spec.in_channels, W0, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W0, W0, 1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W0, W, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU(),
            nn.Conv2d(W, W, 3, padding=1), nn.ReLU())
        self.glob = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(2 * W, 64), nn.ReLU())
        self.g_proj = nn.Linear(64, W)
        self.place_head = nn.Conv2d(W, spec.n_types, 1)
        self.done_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)
        self.value_head = nn.Linear(64, 1)

    def forward(self, obs, mask):
        f = self.body(obs)
        g = self.glob(torch.cat([f.mean((2, 3)), f.amax((2, 3))], dim=1))
        fg = F.relu(f + self.g_proj(g).unsqueeze(-1).unsqueeze(-1))
        place = self.place_head(fg).flatten(1)
        logits = torch.cat([place, self.done_head(g)], dim=1)
        return logits, self.value_head(g).squeeze(1)


def build_policy(spec):
    return Net(spec)

analyses.1: There are no trials yet. The starting network's four seeds scored 0.068, 0.068, 0.258 and 0.068, so training succeeds or fails largely by seed luck, and only gaps much larger than about 0.1 should count. The default recipe gets only 32 PPO updates, so how often the policy updates may matter. To place a brick correctly, the agent has to find the brick's landing layer, which is the highest point under its footprint, and check that every footprint cell is missing at that layer. That is a cross-layer comparison inside each cell followed by an AND over the footprint. A network with only 3x3 convolutions may learn this imprecisely. This round tests three things separately: (A) the recipe alone, with more samples and more frequent smaller updates; (B) a per-cell MLP stem at the same compute; (C) the same stem plus a placement head that takes max and min over each brick's footprint, which gives the head the structure of the landing check.
analyses.2: 0.068 looks like a fixed failure mode. The starting network scored exactly 0.0684 on 3 of 4 seeds, and r1c1, which only had more updates, scored exactly 0.0684 on both seeds. My guess, not yet tested, is that a stuck policy can only build flat or very simple designs and cannot handle stacking or landing height. Both designs with a 1x1 per-cell stem got past it. r1c2 scored 0.10 and 0.39, and r1c3 scored 0.12 and 0.30. Seed-to-seed spread is huge, so r1c2 and r1c3 are tied within noise. The common factor, per-cell nonlinear features before spatial mixing, is the best-supported lesson so far. Escaping the plateau still depends on seed luck. Training takes only 46–87 s, far under the 900 s limit, so FLOPs set the number of samples, not wall time. This round: (1) r1c2 with more samples and updates; (2) r1c2 with a deeper per-cell stem; (3) a new design that judges placements layer by layer, using a learned head shaped like each brick's footprint and taking a soft maximum over layers.
analyses.3: The training recipe matters most. With the per-cell 1x1 stem, the default recipe gave 0.249 (r1c2). Switching to 2 PPO epochs with 128 envs gave 0.625 (r2c1), and both of its seeds (0.71 and 0.54) beat every earlier trial, so the gain is far beyond seed noise. The same recipe change did nothing for the plain baseline (r1c1, 0.068), so the stem and the recipe work together. A third stem layer (r2c2) did not help at the default recipe. Footprint-pooled heads (r1c3, 0.208) roughly matched r1c2 at the default recipe but were never tried with the better recipe. The per-layer model (r2c3, 0.177) was slow and weak. Next: push further along the same recipe axis (fewer epochs for more samples; smaller batches for more updates), and test the footprint head on the improved recipe.
analyses.4: Only one thing clearly worked: the per-cell 1x1 stem (r1c2) trained with 2 PPO epochs, 128 envs and 16 minibatches (r2c1), which scored 0.625 on seeds of 0.71 and 0.54. That is far above the 0.116 baseline mean and well outside the seed noise. Moving away from that recipe in either direction hurt: 4 epochs gave 0.249, 1 epoch gave 0.148, and smaller batches gave 0.224. Results are very sensitive to the recipe, and even the best result may owe something to luck. A third per-cell layer, the footprint-pooled heads and the layer-wise heads all came in at or below 0.25, so I don't see local structural additions as the bottleneck. With 3 trials left, two candidates keep r2c1's network and change one untested recipe setting each. The third makes one cheap change to the network: it feeds global context into the placement head.
